name: Balcarce
shape: geoBoundaries, the department it is named for

climate.koppen_name: Temperate, no dry season, warm summer

climate: Seasons this warm ripen Chardonnay, Cabernet Franc, Sauvignon Blanc, Sémillon and Tempranillo fully without cooking off their freshness.
Chardonnay and Cabernet Franc sit in their sweet spot, so the wines can show the style they are known for.
Pinot Noir is at its warm limit. It can ripen too fast, giving heavy, soft wine that has lost its freshness.
Riesling is at its warm limit. It can ripen too fast, giving heavy, soft wine that has lost its freshness.

soil.rock: Schist, slate and gneiss break into stony, free-draining soil that holds the day's heat. Schist is rich in magnesium and potassium but poor in organic matter and nitrogen.
soil.top: The topsoil holds water well and drains at a steady pace, so vines rarely go thirsty or sit in wet ground. Its pH is close to neutral, so vines take up the nutrients they need easily.

land: Mostly flat. Easy and cheap to farm by machine, but on still nights cold air settles on flat ground, so spring frost is a bigger risk.

winkler: Early and mid-season grapes make good wine.
